context: Three closed-result Rc sharing variants were rejected in diagnostics-61, diagnostics-62 and diagnostics-63. Root-entry omission passed production correctness checks but was rejected by production timing in diagnostics-67. Start this new trial from admitted production behavior, including the original root memo insertion.
hypothesis: A normalization result that is already owned by the existing local memo could be returned as a stable entry index when the caller only needs to borrow it. This may avoid both a polynomial clone and the extra Rc allocation/reference-count work of the rejected variants.
proposed_constraints: Retain the existing memo vector, insertion order, Arc-based eligibility, depth/work limits and arithmetic evaluation order.
Use an owned-result or memo-index return carrier; do not hold references into the vector across recursive calls or insertions.
Share only closed rational/radical forms. Preserve all opaque-atom cloning and reference-count behavior until independently justified.
For a newly computed borrowed closed result, move the value into its existing eligible memo slot. Consuming callers must still obtain an owned value without adding clone work.
Do not introduce persistent caches, a second arena, unsafe references, new dependencies, or a preallocated 512-value table.
Treat larger return values, enum branches, stack use and code size as possible regressions. No speedup or allocation saving is established by this proposal.
required_next_gates: Confirm that every preceding validation/measurement process is terminal before changing any Rust source.
Prepare a separate frozen source tree and retain its exact patch.
Compare all existing 19,140 baseline frontier receipts, including opaque identities, the original root and recursive memo entries, work budgets, strong counts and approximation caches.
Run the independent identity oracle and strict focused scalar checks, then the existing matched time/allocation/size probe before any wider validation.

Reject on unacceptable performance or allocation regressions; preserve every raw sample. Broader production suites, capability/report replay and the unchanged native board gate remain separate requirements.
